summary: Iteration 9 full-stack test. Backend: wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration9.py (16 tests) covering POST/GET /api/actions (auth, 422 validation, persistence, per-user scoping), GET /api/snapshots (no metrics blob, newest-first, no _id), DELETE /api/snapshots/{token} (owner 200, cross-user 404, unknown 404, public read becomes 404), login rate-limit (5 fails -> 401, 6th -> 429 'Too many failed attempts. Try again in ~N min.', success clears counter, lock clears via db.login_attempts), and POST /api/reports/weekly-digest (Claude Sonnet 5, non-empty digest, alerts_count/actions_count/generated_at). Full backend suite = 82/82 passing after I updated two STALE legacy tests that were hammering the admin email with wrong passwords and locking the admin account out (test-only fix). Frontend (Playwright, admin creds): login->dashboard, all 4 finding rows show ASK AI + ACCEPT ACTION, ACCEPT ACTION shows '...', 'Action logged:' toast and swaps to green '✓ LOGGED' pill; Reports weekly digest generates (1155 chars) + COPY shows 'Copied'; Snapshot Manager lists snapshots, revoke removes row (and public link 404s), snapshot-open opens /s/<token> in a new tab and public page renders; theme palette --bg #dbe3d1 / card #f0f3e8 consistent on /, /dashboard, /alerts, /reports, /team; dark toggle swaps both ways; login lockout 429 is surfaced verbatim in the login form error. Zero console/page errors in every run.

minor.issue: Lockout is keyed ONLY on the submitted email (no IP component), so anyone can deliberately lock out any known account (e.g. admin@greensolutions.ai) with 5 bad guesses — account-lockout DoS. This actually happened during regression: legacy tests using the admin email locked the demo admin out. Suggest keying on email+client IP (or lock IP only) and/or exempting/short-locking the demo admin.

No TTL index and no unique index on 'identifier' (server.py:188 creates a plain index). Stale lock rows accumulate forever, and the non-atomic find_one -> upsert can insert duplicate identifier rows under concurrent attempts. Add unique index + TTL (expireAfterSeconds on locked_until/last_failed).

No rate limiting / no cache — each click triggers a paid Sonnet-5 call; a user can spam the button. Also returns 502 on LLM failure with the raw exception string in 'detail' (leaks provider internals).

ui_bugs.issue: Digest text is rendered raw, so markdown from the model shows literal asterisks (e.g. '**Weekly Digest – Green Solutions Portfolio**', '**Next week focus:**'). Either strip '*' or render markdown.

issues: Snapshot list is unbounded (no pagination/scroll cap) — after several shares the section grows very long; consider capping to ~10 with 'show more'.

action_items: Add an IP component (or IP-only) to the login lockout key so a third party cannot lock a known account, and ensure the demo admin cannot be permanently locked.
Add unique + TTL index on db.login_attempts.identifier to avoid duplicate rows and stale locks.
Render/strip markdown in the weekly digest card so '**...**' does not show as literal asterisks.
Optionally throttle/cache POST /api/reports/weekly-digest and stop returning raw LLM exception text in the 502 detail.
Split /app/backend/server.py (894 lines) into routers (auth, portfolio, alerts, reports, snapshots, actions).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py login(): lockout identifier = email only -> targeted account lockout DoS; also `update['count']=0` on lock means a post-expiry failure restarts from 1 while the stale locked_until stays in the doc (harmless but confusing).
server.py:188 db.login_attempts index is non-unique with no TTL; the find_one-then-upsert sequence is not atomic (use a single $inc upsert).
server.py is 894 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline; extract routers.

Auth is localStorage-JWT (pre-existing across iterations 1-8), so the playbook's httpOnly-cookie / CORS-allow-credentials checks do not apply; CORS is allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False which is consistent with that design. bcrypt hash verified to start with $2b$ (backend_test.py::test_bcrypt_hash_format passes).

rca_of_the_issue: The only regression failures (3 failed + 6 errors on the first full run) were caused by pre-existing tests intentionally sending wrong passwords to the admin email; the new iteration-9 lockout then 429'd every subsequent admin login and cascaded into the admin_headers fixture. Root cause is the email-only lockout key combined with stale tests — fixed on the test side; the product-side hardening (IP in the key) is recommended above.
